answer: Give every agent a wood-grain identity: a single willow-shaped keypair whose public half must be countersigned by two peers before any reward unlocks. Each countersignature also pins a timber record of the agent's recent output, so newly cloned keys have no history to sign against and stall at the gate. A horizon window caps how many fresh keys any peer may countersign per epoch. Creating fake identities therefore burns scarce cosignature budget and leaves no verifiable track record, making a wallet swarm less productive than one seasoned worker.
